tasks.task: Diagnose a crash or error and hand back a tested fix

items.when: When you have an error, a log or a wrong result and need the cause proven before the fix
Before changing anything, to rank the suspects and name one check for each
When the main clue is a stack trace or log and you need the first real error under the noise
When a fix is proposed, to see the cause proven with evidence so the fix is not a guess
When reading the code is not enough and you need the values at each step of a real run
When you are guessing at the cause, to follow the actual run and measure first

tasks.task: Review a pull request or code change

items.when: When one pull request or diff needs a review of behaviour, edge cases, risks and tests
When the change is large, to rank the issues by severity and write clear comments
When the change touches sign-in, payments, uploads or user input, to review only that risk
When the change comes with tests, to mark each new behaviour covered or not
When every new pull request should get a risk rating and a draft review to approve
When a change looks neat but may break people who rely on today's behaviour

tasks.task: Check AI-written code before it is merged

items.when: When an AI tool wrote or changed code and it must be checked before a pull request
When the code was written fast, to find the few risks that will hurt later and the smallest fix
When the AI built a whole app, to find leaked keys, open database rules and injection holes
When code grew over many AI sessions, to find duplicate logic and fallbacks that disagree

tasks.task: Fix a bug through a reviewed pull request

items.when: When a bug report, alert or failed build must end as a reviewed, merged fix
First, to turn the report into a repeatable failing case and note what is verified
When you have the repo and want the fix, its proof and the pull request in one run
When the fix should start from a failing test that then stays as the regression test
When the fix is committed, to say what changed, why, and what reviewers should check

tasks.task: Clean up a messy or legacy file without changing what it does

items.when: When one long or tangled file must be cleaned up with tests first and behaviour kept
Before editing, to name the refactoring moves and put them in small safe steps
When the file has no tests, to add a safety net before any line moves
When an AI helper will do the edits, to split the change into small tested steps with rules
When the clean-up is done, to check names, function size and error handling
When tidying and behaviour change are mixed in one step and should be split

tasks.task: Add safety-net and regression tests

items.when: When the code has no tests, to cover units, linked parts and the main user tasks
When the code is hard to test as written, to find the safe places to start
When the code is Python, to prove the new tests fail if the change is broken
When the suite is red after a change, to fix and re-check in capped rounds
When a bug is fixed, to leave a regression test that fails on the old code

tasks.task: Plan a framework, language or library upgrade

items.when: When the app is versions behind and needs a step-by-step plan from its dependency file
When one package jumps a major version, to stage it and test what breaks at each step
Before the plan, to list packages with known weak spots and licence problems
When a file is updated for the new version, to check it against the official docs
When the move is to React 19, to update roots, default props, refs and context
After the upgrade, to keep a weekly list of what is new, open or fixed

tasks.task: Map an unfamiliar codebase for a new owner or developer

items.when: When you inherit a project or must show an owner how their software fits together
When you have the repo, to get entry points, key files and how a request flows
When a new teammate needs a step-by-step tour that links to real files and lines
When the project has no docs, to get a README, a quickstart and a first-run test
When set-up steps exist, to run each one and mark it working or broken

tasks.task: Explain a piece of code in plain words

items.when: When you must understand a function or file before changing it, or explain it to an owner
When the reader is new to code and needs it explained in reading order
When the explanation should be a document with each piece of code beside its reason
When the explanation is abstract, to work one small example by hand

tasks.task: Plan answers to pull request review comments

items.when: When a pull request comes back with many comments and you need what to change and reply
When the comments are on GitHub, to number them and fix the ones you pick
When the same pull request should be reviewed, fixed and signed off with proof in one run

tasks.task: Write, test or explain a regular expression

items.when: When you need a pattern for postcodes, order numbers or dates, tested on real examples
Before testing, to list the odd inputs the pattern must accept or reject
When the pattern guards money or identity data, to write its rules down and hold it to them

tasks.task: Parse a log or messy export into a clean table

items.when: When a log or text export must become a CSV, with odd lines counted and not lost
When each line needs a tested pattern to pull out its fields
When the file's encoding, separators or format cause read errors
When the parser will be reused, to add tests for normal, odd and broken lines

tasks.task: Write validation rules for form or API input

items.when: When you have the code, to find every place outside data enters and how it is checked
When a field has a fixed format, such as a postcode, phone number or order number
When you need the empty, too-long and wrong-type cases each rule must handle

tasks.task: Run a health check on an inherited codebase

items.when: When a new owner inherits a codebase, a key developer leaves, or every three months
When you need the debt that slows the team ranked, with cost and small fixes
When the structure itself is in doubt, to list design improvements and pick one
When the codebase is large and old, to plan making it readable and bounded step by step
After the first check, to find new debt each month and confirm last month's clean-up
When the risk notes list bugs but not what happens when a part fails

tasks.task: Check code for security gaps and leaked secrets

items.when: When the code is Python, JavaScript, TypeScript or Go, to rank security gaps with fixes
When keys may sit in the repo or its history, to find them and plan rotation
When the risk is in packages, to list known weak spots and licence issues
When one change is in question, to check input handling and permission checks

tasks.task: Fix code that works locally but fails on the server

items.when: When it runs on a laptop and fails live, to compare versions, config and data in order
When errors are tracked in Sentry, to sum up the recent issues and key details first
When the failure is a timeout or a flaky outside call, to add retries and limits
When the failure is in a GitHub Actions run, to read the log and fix the workflow file

tasks.task: Find and fix slow code or a slow query

items.when: When something is slow and nobody knows where, to measure CPU, memory and I/O hot spots
When the fix should land as a pull request with before and after timings
When one SQL query is the slow part, to find why and add indexes where needed
When the plan is to rewrite before measuring where the time goes

tasks.task: Set up CI and checks that run on every push

items.when: When the project needs a pipeline file with test and deploy stages for its stack
When formatting, type and test checks should run before each commit
After a change, to run the project's checks, fix real failures and say what did not run
When the pipeline fails, to find the root cause in the log

tasks.task: Write the README, code docs and decision records

items.when: When the code has no docs, to write docstrings, a README and usage guides that match it
When a design choice was made, to record why and what was passed over
Before publishing, to find claims in the docs that no longer match the code
When docs go stale, to fix old pages and flag broken steps each month

tasks.task: Sort out a Git tangle and write clean commits

items.when: When a merge, rebase or branch has gone wrong and needs untangling safely
When changes are staged and need a short message that says what changed and why
When the branch is ready and reviewers need to know what to look at

tasks.task: Prepare and check a release

items.when: Before each release, to get a go or no-go, the version, a changelog and a rollback plan
When the release has migrations or config changes, to list the real deploy risks
When one late change is going into the release and needs a second look

tasks.task: Make the repo ready for AI coding agents

items.when: When coding agents will work in the repo, to score it and write project instructions
When an instructions file exists, to check it has real commands and no guesses
When an agent takes on a change, to give it a test list and small steps
When the change should be made and tested inside the project by a coding agent

always.when: Before any change, to list the cases to check, smallest first
After any code change, to run the project's own checks before you call it done

helpers.when: When the fix or refactor needs a test plan, browser tests or a regression checklist
When the problem is in the pipeline, the containers or the server setup, not the code
When the review finds a security hole that needs a proper threat model and fix
When the bug or slowness sits in the schema, a migration or the queries
When the health check shows the structure is the problem and needs a redesign
When the codebase map must become full docs for users or other teams

gaps: No library item writes, tests or explains a regular expression; only the kit prompt does
No library item turns a log file or messy text export into a table with odd lines counted
No library item moves jQuery to plain JavaScript or converts a JavaScript file to TypeScript
No library item plans a Laravel, Symfony, Django, Rails, Express, Vue or Angular upgrade; only React and Expo are covered
No library item plans a move to a supported PHP, Python or Node version, or tests old and new versions side by side in CI
No library item compares local and server set-ups (versions, config, env values, data) for a bug that only fails live
No library item diagnoses a bug that happens only sometimes, such as a race or timing fault
No library item writes validation rules for form or API input
No library item plans replacing an unmaintained library with a supported one
No library item writes a first-week plan for a new developer joining a codebase
